concepts.name: Asymptotic notation beyond big-O
concepts.gloss: Ω gives an asymptotic lower bound, Θ a tight bound and o a strictly smaller order of growth, defined alongside big-O by comparing a function with a constant multiple of another for all large inputs.

concepts.name: Logarithms and binary logarithm
concepts.gloss: The logarithm log_b x is the exponent to which b must be raised to give x, with lg x = log_2 x counting the bits needed to write x, and log of a product being a sum of logs.

concepts.name: Floor and ceiling functions
concepts.gloss: ⌊x⌋ is the largest integer not above x and ⌈x⌉ the smallest integer not below x.

concepts.name: Binary representation of integers
concepts.gloss: A nonnegative integer below 2^n is written as n bits b_i with value Σ b_i 2^i, and two's complement represents signed integers in a fixed width by taking the top bit as -2^{w-1}.

concepts.name: Radix representation and digits
concepts.gloss: An integer is written in base B as digits d_i in {0,…,B-1} with value Σ d_i B^i, so that splitting into digits and recombining is the same as cutting the bit string into fields.

concepts.name: Schoolbook multiplication and carries
concepts.gloss: Multiplying n-digit numbers by multiplying every pair of digits and adding shifted partial products with carries takes O(n^2) digit operations, while adding two n-bit numbers with carries takes O(n).

concepts.name: Divide-and-conquer and recurrences
concepts.gloss: A problem is split into smaller subproblems whose costs obey a recurrence T(n)=aT(n/b)+f(n), solved by unrolling levels and summing a geometric series, as in Karatsuba's O(n^{log_2 3}) multiplication.

concepts.name: Fast Fourier transform and FFT multiplication
concepts.gloss: The FFT evaluates a polynomial at the roots of unity of a power-of-two order in O(n log n) operations by recursing on even and odd coefficients, and multiplies polynomials by evaluating, multiplying pointwise and interpolating.

concepts.name: Mathematical induction and proof by cases
concepts.gloss: A statement for all n is proved by establishing a base case and showing that each case follows from earlier ones.

concepts.name: Sets, subsets and Cartesian products
concepts.gloss: Finite sets, their subsets, intersections and sizes, and the product A×B of tuples, with a vector indexed by a set recording one value for each element.

concepts.name: Functions, bijections and permutations
concepts.gloss: A bijection of a finite set onto itself is a permutation, permutations compose and have inverses, and a function applied to every index rearranges an array.

concepts.name: Modular arithmetic and congruences
concepts.gloss: Integers are compared by their remainder on division by n, with addition and multiplication of remainders well defined, and an element is invertible modulo n exactly when it shares no factor with n.

concepts.name: Primes, divisibility and coprimality
concepts.gloss: Divisibility, prime numbers, prime powers and the gcd, with two integers coprime when their gcd is 1.

concepts.name: Rational numbers and exact fractions
concepts.gloss: A rational number is a ratio of integers, and a dyadic rational is one whose denominator is a power of two so that it has a finite binary expansion.

concepts.name: Finite fields and the field F_2
concepts.gloss: The field with elements 0 and 1 in which addition is XOR and multiplication is AND, so that linear algebra works over it as over the real numbers.

concepts.name: Vectors, matrices and linear maps
concepts.gloss: Vectors in a field's n-space, matrices as linear maps, their products, inverses and diagonal and identity forms, and a linear combination as a sum of scalar multiples.

concepts.name: Rank, basis and dimension
concepts.gloss: A basis is a linearly independent spanning set whose size is the dimension, and the rank of a matrix is the dimension of the space spanned by its columns.

concepts.name: Gaussian elimination
concepts.gloss: Row operations reduce a matrix to triangular form, expressing an invertible matrix as a product of elementary row-operation matrices.

concepts.name: Inner product, norm and orthonormal basis
concepts.gloss: The inner product Σ u_i v_i measures orthogonality, a norm assigns a length to a vector (the max norm being its largest entry in absolute value), and an orthonormal basis consists of mutually orthogonal unit vectors.

concepts.name: Roots of unity and Euler's formula
concepts.gloss: The complex numbers e^{2πik/n} satisfy z^n=1, lie on the unit circle, and have power sums Σ_k z^{jk} equal to 0 unless n divides j.

concepts.name: Summation and product notation
concepts.gloss: Σ and Π denote sums and products over an index range, with index manipulations and the Kronecker delta selecting one term.

concepts.name: Newton's method
concepts.gloss: Repeatedly replacing an estimate x by x - f(x)/f'(x) converges quadratically to a root of f, giving division and square roots from multiplication at doubling precision.

concepts.name: Integer division with remainder
concepts.gloss: Every integer a and positive b give a unique quotient q=⌊a/b⌋ and remainder r=a-bq with 0≤r<b, and the integer square root is ⌊√a⌋.

concepts.name: Lexicographic order
concepts.gloss: Tuples are ordered by comparing first coordinates, then second, and so on, which lists a multi-index array in row-major order.

concepts.name: Arrays, records and matrix transposition
concepts.gloss: An array holds elements at integer indices, a matrix is stored row by row and its transpose swaps row and column indices.

concepts.name: Turing machine running time and model conventions
concepts.gloss: The running time of a Turing machine is the number of steps on the worst input of each length, differing from a RAM that reaches any memory cell in unit time, and linear passes and sorting by merging on tapes are standard.

background.summary: Undergraduate computer science: algorithms and complexity through big-O analysis, recurrences and divide-and-conquer (Karatsuba, FFT-based polynomial multiplication, usually met at the level of the standard recursive FFT), discrete mathematics (modular arithmetic, primes and gcd, sets, functions and permutations, induction), and introductory linear algebra (matrices, rank, bases, inner products, Gaussian elimination, over the reals and probably F_2). Also the basics of complex numbers and Turing machines with multiple tapes. The reader has not studied abstract algebra such as quotient rings or tensor products, finite-field theory beyond F_2, numerical analysis of rounding errors, or the research literature on integer multiplication (Schönhage–Strassen, Fürer, Harvey–van der Hoeven), and has not seen Bluestein, Nussbaumer polynomial transforms or Gaussian resampling.
